what: Margin rubric. What a correct answer to one lesson question needs and what each score means, written by Margin on a teacher's key. Keyed by a fingerprint of the question; no question text, no student work, no names.

rubric.asks: Why a republic's constitution wouldn't work once Texas became a state
rubric.note: Warmup: students speculate before learning about the Convention of 1845; any reasoned idea about the change from republic to state counts.

bands.means: Gives an idea about why a state needs a different constitution, with a reason behind it.
Gives an idea about why a new constitution was needed, but no reason behind it.
Talks about Texas joining the United States without saying why a new constitution was needed.
Mentions Texas, statehood, or constitutions only, with no answer to the question.

examples.answer: A republic runs itself, but a state has to follow the U.S. government too. So the old rules would not match the new job.
I think the old constitution did not fit anymore so they had to write a new one.
Texas joined the United States in 1845 and became a state.
